heading: Prepare a coordinated tax-planning agenda for a complex household
body:
Owners with several entities, properties, or income sources need a shared planning agenda. A strategy considered in one company can affect cash, reporting, or decisions elsewhere. Start with an ownership map and a list of the household’s major decisions before discussing individual deductions.

Bring the latest financial statements, prior returns, payroll, property schedules, existing elections, carryforward information, and material changes expected during the year. Identify which adviser maintains each record. If different professionals prepare related returns, ask how information and implementation responsibilities will be coordinated through secure channels.

For a fictional household buying a building while admitting a business partner, the relevant questions extend beyond the purchase price. Ownership, financing, compensation, distributions, agreement terms, property use, and cash reserves need to be considered together. A single strategy estimate should not stand in for that coordinated review.

Leave the planning meeting with a dated action list. Each item should show the decision, required evidence, responsible professional, owner task, deadline, and completion record. Ask what is included in the engagement and which additional services need a separate scope. Clear implementation responsibilities make the advice more useful.
